```{r}
bird_breeding_selected <- breeding_site_locations |>
  select(Site, Longitude, Latitude)

gt(bird_breeding_selected)
```

```{r}
bird_breeding_selected <- breeding_site_locations |>
  select(Site, Longitude, Latitude) |>
  distinct()

gt(bird_breeding_selected)
```

```{r}
bird_breeding_selected <- breeding_site_locations |>
  select(Site, Longitude, Latitude) |>
  distinct() |>
  rename(Breeding_Longitude = Longitude, Breeding_Latitude = Latitude)

gt(bird_breeding_selected)
```



```{r}
bird_migration_selected <- migratory_connectivity_dataset |>
  select(Site, winterLongitude, winterLatitude, pslon, pslat, iblon, iblat, awestlon, awestlat) |>
  distinct() |>
  rename(Winter_Longitude = winterLongitude, Winter_Latitude = winterLatitude, Stopover_Longitude = pslon, Stopover_Latitude = pslat, Iberian_Longitude = iblon, Iberian_Laritude = iblat, Westmost_Longtitude = awestlon, Westmost_Latitude = awestlat)
gt(bird_migration_selected)
```

# selecting for row of only Dartmoor

```{r}
bird_breeding_dartmoor <- bird_breeding_selected |> filter(Site == "Dartmoor")

gt(bird_breeding_dartmoor)
```

# selecting for rows except Dartmoor

```{r}
bird_breeding_not_dartmoor <- bird_breeding_selected |> filter(Site != "Dartmoor")

gt(bird_breeding_not_dartmoor)
```

# selecting for rows where breeding longitude is greater than 10

```{r}
bird_breeding_long_10 <- bird_breeding_selected |> filter(Breeding_Longitude > 10)

gt(bird_breeding_long_10)
```

# bird breeding rows excluding Spain

```{r}
bird_breeding_exc <- bird_breeding_selected |> filter(Site != "Spain")

gt(bird_breeding_exc)
```

# bird migration exlcuding Spain

```{r}
bird_migration_exc <- bird_migration_selected |> filter(Site != "Spain")

gt(head(bird_migration_exc))
```

# Part 2 -- start below

# group the migration frame by site column

```{r}
bird_migration_grouped <- bird_migration_exc |> group_by(Site)
```

# glimpse function used to visualise the grouped data frame has worked

```{r}
glimpse(bird_migration_grouped)
```

# used to make a new summarised data frame where have collected the max values of stopover latitude at the sites

```{r}
lat_df <- bird_migration_grouped |>
  summarise(Highest_Lat_Stopover = max(Stopover_Latitude, na.rm = TRUE))

gt(lat_df)
```

# now collecting max, min and mean as well

```{r}
lat_df <- bird_migration_grouped |>
  summarise(
    Highest_Lat_Stopover = max(Stopover_Latitude, na.rm = TRUE),
    Lowest_Lat_Stopover = min(Stopover_Latitude, na.rm = TRUE),
    Mean_Lat_Stopover = mean(Stopover_Latitude, na.rm = TRUE),
    Highest_Lat_Winter = max(Winter_Latitude, na.rm = TRUE),
    Lowest_Lat_Winter = min(Winter_Latitude, na.rm = TRUE),
    Mean_Lat_Winter = mean(Winter_Latitude, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

gt(lat_df)
```

```{r}
bird_migration_summary <- bird_migration_grouped |>
  summarise(
    Stopover_Latitude = median(Stopover_Latitude, na.rm = TRUE),
    Stopover_Longitude = median(Stopover_Longitude, na.rm = TRUE), 
    Iberian_Latitude = median(Iberian_Laritude, na.rm = TRUE),
    Iberian_Longitude = median(Iberian_Longitude, na.rm = TRUE),
    Westmost_Latitude = median(Westmost_Latitude, na.rm = TRUE),
    Westmost_Longitude = median(Westmost_Longtitude, na.rm = TRUE),
    Winter_Latitude = median(Winter_Latitude, na.rm = TRUE),
    Winter_Longitude = median(Winter_Longitude, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

gt(bird_migration_summary)
```


```{r}
df_dept <- read_csv("data/depts.csv")
df_score <- read_csv("data/scores.csv")
```

# joins two data frames -- is a join, which allows us to combine two data frames into one, assuming they have a column in common --

```{r}
gt(df_dept)
```

# joins two data frames -- is a join, which allows us to combine two data frames into one, assuming they have a column in common --

```{r}
gt(df_score)
```

# joins connected data frames (which contain more than 1 data frame) together, retaining all columns by adding in NA for where there is no data -- is a full join, which retains all of the rows from both data frames, adding NA where no data is available --

```{r}
full_join_example <- full_join(df_dept, df_score)
```

```{r}
gt(full_join_example)
```

# is an inner join, which only retains rows for individuals which are in both data frames

```{r}
inner_join_example <- inner_join(df_dept, df_score)
```

```{r}
gt(inner_join_example)
```

# is a left join, which retains all the rows in the first data frame and adds data from the second data frame where available, adding NA where it is not

```{r}
left_join_example <- left_join(df_dept, df_score)
```

```{r}
gt(left_join_example)
```

# is a right join, which retains all the rows in the second data frame and adds data from the first data frame where available, adding NA where it is not

```{r}
right_join_example <- right_join(df_dept, df_score)
```

```{r}
gt(right_join_example)
```

```{r}
combined_bird_data <- full_join(bird_breeding_exc, bird_migration_summary)

gt(combined_bird_data)
```

# all of the above are in the wide format!!!


# converting from wide to long format:

```{r}
combined_bird_piv <- combined_bird_data |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = ends_with(c("Longitude", "Latitude")),
    names_sep = "_",
    names_to = c("Location_Type", ".value")
  )

gt(combined_bird_piv)
```

# gt function makes a tablw to visualise data


```{r}
gt(df_dept)
```

# to only get those for English and Maths:

```{r}
keep_depts <- c("Maths", "English")

df_eng_maths <- df_dept |>
  filter(Department %in% keep_depts)

gt(df_eng_maths)
```

# generating 2 sub-sets of the combined_bird_priv data frame, based on season (spring and autumn data)

```{r}
spring_vals <- c("Breeding", "Stopover", "Winter")
autumn_vals <- c("Breeding", "Iberian", "Westmost", "Winter")

spring_data <- combined_bird_piv |>
  filter(Location_Type %in% spring_vals)

autumn_data <- combined_bird_piv |>
  filter(Location_Type %in% autumn_vals)
```

```{r}
write_csv(spring_data, "output/birds_spring.csv")
write_csv(autumn_data, "output/birds_autumn.csv")
```

```{r}
gt(spring_data)
```

```{r}
ggplot(spring_data)
```

```{r}
ggplot(
  spring_data,
  aes(x = Longitude, y = Latitude)
)
```

```{r}
my_data_frame <- tibble(
  fruit = c("apple", "pear", "banana"),
  length = c(22, 30, 55),
  weight = c(150, 165, 170)
)

gt(my_data_frame)
```

#To plot this data as a scatter plot, with length on the x axis and weight on the y axis

```{r}
ggplot(my_data_frame, aes(x = length, y = weight)) +
  geom_point()
```

```{r}
ggplot(spring_data, aes(x = Longitude, y = Latitude)) +
  geom_point()
```

# function annotation_borders() = add geographical country borders to a scatter plot representing a map
# function coord_quickmap() = keeps shape of the plot consistent so the map isn’t skewed

```{r}
ggplot(
  spring_data,
  aes(x = Longitude, y = Latitude)
) +
  geom_point() +
  annotation_borders(linewidth = 0.2) +
  coord_quickmap()
```

# to find min and max longitude and latitude us min(), max(). pull() pulls a single column from the data frame

#finding min longtitude below, and the rest...:

```{r}
min_lon <- spring_data |>
  pull(Longitude) |>
  min()

print(min_lon)
```

```{r}
max_lon <- spring_data |>
  pull(Longitude) |>
  max()

print(max_lon)
```


```{r}
min_lat <- spring_data |>
  pull(Latitude) |>
  min()

print(min_lat)
```

```{r}
max_lat <- spring_data |>
  pull(Latitude) |>
  max()

print(max_lat)
```



# important as allows to then figure out what to set axis limits to, so can zoom in on graph to only contain the parts where the points actually are present

# set x axis limits with coord_quickmap() function:

```{r}
ggplot(
  spring_data,
  aes(x = Longitude, y = Latitude)
) +
  geom_point() +
  annotation_borders(linewidth = 0.2) +
  coord_quickmap(xlim = c(min_lon - 2, max_lon + 2))
```

# same but now for y axis and x axis

```{r}
ggplot(
  spring_data,
  aes(x = Longitude, y = Latitude)
) +
  geom_point() +
  annotation_borders(linewidth = 0.2) +
  coord_quickmap(
    ylim = c(min_lat - 2, max_lat + 2), xlim = c(min_lon -2, max_lon + 2)
    )
```

# to increase the size of the points themselves increase geom_point(size=bigger number)

```{r}
ggplot(
  spring_data,
  aes(x = Longitude, y = Latitude)
) +
  geom_point(size=3) +
  annotation_borders(linewidth = 0.2) +
  coord_quickmap(
    xlim = c(min_lon - 2, max_lon + 2),
    ylim = c(min_lat - 2, max_lat + 2)
  )
```

# aes() function controls how variables in the data are mapped to visual properties of the plot. Previously mapped Longitude to the x-axis and Latitude to the y-axis but can also map variables to colour, shape and many other visual properties

```{r}
gt(spring_data)
```

# set colour by the site column (colour = site) with aes() function

```{r}
ggplot(
  spring_data,
  aes(x = Longitude, y = Latitude, color = Site)
) +
  geom_point(size=3) +
  annotation_borders(linewidth = 0.2) +
  coord_quickmap(
    xlim = c(min_lon - 2, max_lon + 2),
    ylim = c(min_lat - 2, max_lat + 2)
  )
```

# including (shape = Location_Type) within aes() function so shape set by location type

```{r}
ggplot(
  spring_data,
  aes(x = Longitude, y = Latitude, color = Site, shape = Location_Type)
) +
  geom_point(size=3) +
  annotation_borders(linewidth = 0.2) +
  coord_quickmap(
    xlim = c(min_lon - 2, max_lon + 2),
    ylim = c(min_lat - 2, max_lat + 2)
  )
```

# 1- use ggtitle() to give graph a title, 2- use xlab() and ylab() to give the axis labels

# theme_minimal() can be used to apply the ggplot minimal theme to the plots, this changes the default plot appearance (is a personal preference to apply a theme)



```{r}
ggplot(
  spring_data,
  aes(x = Longitude, y = Latitude, color = Site, shape = Location_Type)
) +
  geom_point(size  = 3) +
  annotation_borders(linewidth = 0.2) +
  coord_quickmap(
    xlim = c(min_lon - 2, max_lon + 2),
    ylim = c(min_lat - 2, max_lat + 2)
  ) +
  ggtitle("Pied Flycatcher Spring Migration Routes") +
  xlab("Longitude (°)") +
  ylab("Latitude (°)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

# can add paths to connect points of migration locations by using geom_path() function, grouping the points by breeding site, and by adding the argument aes(group = Site)

```{r}
ggplot(
  spring_data,
  aes(x = Longitude, y = Latitude, color = Site, shape = Location_Type)
) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  annotation_borders(linewidth = 0.2) +
  coord_quickmap(
    xlim = c(min_lon - 2, max_lon + 2),
    ylim = c(min_lat - 2, max_lat + 2)
  ) +
  geom_path(aes(group = Site)) +
  ggtitle("Pied Flycatcher Spring Migration Routes") +
  xlab("Longitude (°)") +
  ylab("Latitude (°)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
min_lon <- autumn_data |>
  pull(Longitude) |>
  min()

max_lon <- autumn_data |>
  pull(Longitude) |>
  max()

min_lat <- autumn_data |>
  pull(Latitude) |>
  min()

max_lat <- autumn_data |>
  pull(Latitude) |>
  max()

ggplot(
  autumn_data,
  aes(x = Longitude, y = Latitude, color = Site, shape = Location_Type)
) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  annotation_borders(linewidth = 0.2) +
  coord_quickmap(
    xlim = c(min_lon - 2, max_lon + 2),
    ylim = c(min_lat - 2, max_lat + 2)
  ) +
  geom_path(aes(group = Site)) +
  ggtitle("Pied Flycatcher Autumn Migration Routes") +
  xlab("Longitude (°)") +
  ylab("Latitude (°)") +
  theme_minimal()
```
